result.theme: Theme B — Vendor all FigureImage hotlinks locally (fix broken/fragile external Wikimedia images)
result.summary: All 27 <FigureImage> instances across 20 section/module files hotlink external Wikimedia thumbnail URLs (https://upload.wikimedia.org/...); public/ contains only PWA icons. A live HTTP audit (curl range-GET with a browser UA to defeat Wikimedia 429 rate-limiting) found 11 of the 27 are dead (HTTP 404) and the other 16, while currently 200/206, are fragile hotlinks subject to thumbnail-URL churn and rate-limiting. The fix is to download every image into a new public/figures/ directory under a stable filename and repoint each src to a BASE_URL-relative local path (src={`${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}figures/<file>`}); FigureImage already renders caption/attribution/sourceUrl from props, so attribution is preserved verbatim — only the src attribute changes, and the original Wikimedia File: page stays in sourceUrl for provenance.

result.theme: Section numbering standardization (derive Part.Section from curriculum order; delete stale per-module numbers)
result.summary: The 3-module→5-Part consolidation left every transmission-domain module file carrying its OLD per-module numbering, which now contradicts the curriculum spine: Transformers uses "1.x" but is curriculum 3.4; LumpedDistributed uses "2.x" but is 5.1; TransmissionLines uses "3.x" but is 5.2; Transients uses "4.x" but is 5.3; Antennas uses "5.x" but is 4.4. These stale numbers appear as user-facing h2 headings ("3.2 — Reflections…"), eyebrow paragraphs ("Section 5.3"), LabStation number= props, the LabStation unit test, and banner code comments. The circuits and em sections are clean (only image-attribution dashes are false positives), and Part-level numbering already derives correctly from PARTS[].number in Sidebar/CourseLanding. Fix: add a getSectionNumber(id) helper to curriculum.ts that computes "<Part.number>.<1-based index within Part>" from PARTS, then feed it (with a sub-index for in-section headings) at every call site and delete the hardcoded numbers.

result.summary: On the CourseLanding page (route `/`), each Part card lists its section names as plain, non-interactive text inside `<li>` elements, while only a single "Start Part N" link at the bottom of the card is clickable. This theme makes every individual section name a react-router `<Link>` deep-linking to `SECTIONS[id].route`, so users can jump straight to any section from the landing page. `Link` is already imported in CourseLanding.tsx, so no new import is required; the change is localized to the section-list `<li>` render and needs a focus ring for keyboard a11y.

Desired hover/focus visual treatment: the proposal uses hover color + underline + a focus ring matching the AiTutor convention. Confirm whether underline-on-hover fits the intended landing aesthetic, or whether it should match the sidebar NavLink hover-background style instead.

result.theme: Theme G — EM chart-quality fixes (PhysicsChart numeric/log/dual-axis)
result.summary: The shared `PhysicsChart` wrapper (src/em/components/common/PhysicsChart.tsx) renders a single linear-y recharts LineChart and is consumed in exactly 4 places across the EM domain (coulomb, gauss, em-wave ×2). Three systemic defects recur: (1) every data generator stringifies the x-value via toFixed/toString, forcing recharts onto a categorical (band) x-axis with distorted spacing; (2) inverse-square data (coulomb F, gauss E) is plotted on a linear y-axis so it spikes then visually flattens; (3) gauss mixes two different-unit series (constant flux N·m²/C and E-field N/C) on one shared "Value" axis. The fix is to extend PhysicsChart with an optional numeric x-type, optional log y-scale, and an optional second y-axis (all natively supported by the installed recharts 3.8.1), then update each call site's data-gen to keep x numeric and route series to the right axis/scale.

changes.proposed: Add an optional `axis?: 'left' | 'right'` field to ChartLine (default 'left'). Extend PhysicsChartProps with: `xType?: 'number' | 'category'` (default 'category' to preserve current behavior, callers opt into 'number'); `xDomain?: [number | string, number | string]` (optional, e.g. ['dataMin','dataMax'] or [0,'dataMax']); `yScale?: 'linear' | 'log'` (default 'linear'); `yDomain?: [number | string, number | string]` (needed because log scale requires an explicit positive domain, e.g. ['auto','auto'] or [min, 'dataMax']); and `y2Label?: string` + `y2Scale?: 'linear' | 'log'` to enable a secondary right-hand y-axis. Change `data` element type to `Record<string, number | string>[]` (already is) — fine.
changes.rationale: Component must expose numeric-x, log-y, and dual-axis options before any call site can be fixed; defaults keep the other (non-EM) usages byte-for-byte unchanged.
